newsitem.title: JORDAN: Arafat in Jordan to seek King Hussein's support.
newsitem.headline: Arafat in Jordan to seek King Hussein's support.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat arrived in Amman on Saturday to seek King Hussein's help in overcoming hurdles in peace talks with Israel, officials said.

Witnesses said Arafat, who flew in with Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti after talks in Gaza on bilateral cooperation, was met by King Hussein and given a full state welcome by a bedouin guard of honour.

Arafat, who attacked Israel's unilateral decision on Friday to hand over only nine percent more of the West Bank in the first of three pullbacks, wants the monarch to put pressure on Israel to implement signed peace accords.
Palestinians are also angry at Israeli plans to start building 6,5000 homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem.
"I want to consult him (King Hussein) and to ask for his assistance to overcome the difficulties we are facing by the Israelis, including settlement in Jerusalem," Arafat said earlier in Gaza.

The monarch's intervention helped in January to seal a long-delayed accord on Israeli troop withdrawal from 80 percent of the West Bank town of Hebron and a timetable for further redeployment from the West Bank.
